text:
I am filing this complaint to report systemic misconduct by PNC Bank regarding the operation of my checking account, which was lawfully tendered and opened under a signature card agreement with the intent that it function as a credit account backed by the United States Treasury. This account has been improperly administered, violating both contractual obligations and federal credit procedures. 

Specifically, I submitted a rental lease security instrument to the account, which was dishonored without legal justification. This lease was intended as a credit instrument and special deposit. The bank refused to credit the account appropriately and has since failed to account for this deposit under proper double-entry credit procedures. The matter is under investigation. 

In addition, multiple checks and other commercial instruments submitted to the account have also been mishandled, not properly posted as credits, and the debit card fails to reflect the true credit-backed nature of the account. PNC is treating all transactions as debits without acknowledging the account 's commercial structure or the lawful credit backing of the United States under the Federal Reserve Act 16 and 12 U.S.C. 411.

I have notified PNC via lawful notices, including commercial assignments and ledger corrections, yet these were ignored or dishonored. Their failure to apply correct accounting is a violation of : UCC 3-104 and 3-603 ( Negotiable Instruments and Discharge ) Federal Reserve Act 16 Truth in Lending Act Breach of fiduciary responsibility and contract ( via the signed Signature Card ) I request that the CFPB : Investigate PNCs systemic dishonor of lawful commercial instruments ; Ensure the account is reconciled to reflect proper credit ledger postings ; Confirm that the account and debit card function as a credit-backed account under public credit ; Hold PNC accountable for all dishonored instruments and return all denied credits. 

The bank 's actions amount to ledger fraud, fiduciary neglect, and denial of lawful credit access. I am requesting a full remedy and oversight from the CFPB to bring the account into lawful compliance.

text:
I filed a Regulation E unauthorized transaction dispute with Navy Federal Credit Union and more than 10 business days have passed with no provisional credit and no written notice of delay. Under 12 CFR 1005.11 ( c ), the bank is required to either ( 1 ) resolve the dispute within 10 business days, or ( 2 ) issue a provisional credit if the investigation is not yet complete. text:
In XXXX 2025, I was a XXXX monthly subscription customer. XXXX incorrectly charged me an unexpected increase of {$200.00} for the Loss Damage Waiver ( LDW ). I immediately contacted XXXX and was told by their customer service that this amount would be refunded and that the billing issue was a system error, not my fault. 

However, XXXX never issued the refund they promised. Since the overcharge remained unresolved for weeks, I filed a legitimate dispute with American Express, which was later resolved in my favor by Amex after their investigation. 

After the dispute was resolved, XXXX placed me on their internal Blocked List, refused to renew my subscription, and demanded that I reverse the chargebackeven though the chargeback was the result of their own billing error and failure to issue the refund they promised in writing. 

XXXX also provided conflicting explanations to different parties : In emails to me, they acknowledged the charge was a system error and promised a refund. 
In their XXXX response, they claimed the charge was valid and insisted I owed them money. 
They also told XXXX that they had a discount workaround, but they never communicated this to me before the dispute and never applied any recurring discount on my invoices. 

Their actions appear retaliatory, misleading, and harmful to consumers. Blocking my account and demanding reversal of a valid chargeback is inappropriate and has disrupted my transportation plans. Their accounting department has ignored my emails for weeks. 

I believe this behavior constitutes unfair billing practices, retaliation for filing a chargeback, and misrepresentation of charges.

sub_issue: Company closed your account
text:
I am submitting this complaint because Chase closed my credit card account unfairly and without properly reviewing my situation. I am a college student and rely on this card, and what Chase did feels extremely unreasonable and harmful to me. 

I had Chase for about five to six months and only ever missed one payment. I recently filed a few disputes with Chases customer claims department because I was confused about some transactions and believed some were unauthorized. I filed these disputes through their proper channels and followed everything they told me to do. No one ever warned me, contacted me, or told me that filing disputes could harm my account or be considered abuse. If they had said anything, I would have been more careful, but they didnt give me any information besides processing my claims normally. 

Even after the disputes, I still paid Chase {$300.00} early and in full to settle everything and stay on good terms. I acted in good faith, and I believed my account was fine. 

The very next day after filing my CFPB report, Chase sent me a letter saying they are closing my account due to a pattern of abuse of our claims process. This makes no sense and feels extremely unfair. I used the claims process exactly the way Chase told me to. I did not commit fraud. I did not try to take advantage of the system. I simply filed disputes for things I believed were wrong on my account. 

The letter from Chase felt automated and did not reflect the actual situation. I was never given a chance to explain myself, speak to a representative, or even understand what was happening. I was never told my account was at risk of closure despite calling and communicating with Chase multiple times. 

I feel punished for using the claims system they provided. I also paid them {$300.00} even after filing the disputes, which shows I acted responsibly. Closing my account after I paid early makes me feel like Chase took my money and immediately shut me out. 

This whole situation is extremely stressful because I am a student, I depend on this card, and I try very hard to keep my finances clean and responsible. Chases sudden decision has affected my trust in them and has made me anxious about my financial stability.

sub_issue: Payment process
text:
I made a duplicate monthly payment on my mortgage. ( I set up auto-draft with my mortgage servicer before I could cancel an automatic payment from my bank -- both cleared. ) I immediately requested the mortgage servicer reverse or refund one of the duplicate payments.

The servicer took several days to research the matter before providing me a letter requesting my personal bank statements to provide evidence that the payments had cleared. This is unnecessary and not possible. First, because one payment was made recently outside of a statement period so no statement exists yet for that payment, and second, the servicer has already credited the payments as having cleared -- there is no need to examine my private bank account for whether payments were made.

I repeated my request to have one duplicate payment refunded to which I received a " resolution letter '' that specified an arbitrary " 15-day funds validation period ''. If I wanted a refund sooner than that waiting period, I needed to provide my personal bank statements. Once the 15-day waiting period had expired or after my personal bank accounts were examined, I could request a paper check mailed within 5-7 days. If no action was taken on my part after this letter, my duplicate payment would be applied to my next monthly mortgage payment. 

These processes and policies are arbitrary, unnecessary, and punitive in the financial burden it places on a borrower who overpaid the lender. Case in point, I made a duplicate payment on a credit card balance to XXXX XXXX, and within XXXX XXXX days of my request, XXXXXXXX XXXX reversed the payment to my checking account -- no " validation period '', no personal bank statements, and no paper checks.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint to report a mortgage loan originator engaging in non-compliant advertising practices in violation of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.24. 

On XXXX, XXXX XXXX, [ NMLS # XXXX ], distributed an email blast to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX membership that advertised specific interest rates without disclosing the corresponding APRs. 

The email stated : Here is a sampling of rates based on an 80 % purchase loan amount of $ XXXX. APR varies depending on points/lender costs. These rates reflect discount points less than .25 %, FICO XXXX on a Primary/2nd Home purchase. 

It then listed the following note rates : 30 YR Fixed 6.375 % XXXX ARM 5.875 % XXXX ARM 5.750 % This communication does not include the required APR disclosures alongside the advertised note rates. Instead, it only includes a vague disclaimer that APR varies, which does not satisfy federal disclosure requirements. 

As you know, Regulation Z requires that any advertisement of a specific interest rate must also state the APR with equal prominence. By omitting the APR, this advertisement is misleading to consumers and real estate professionals who may rely on this information. 

Evidence Provided : A copy of the email sent to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX distribution list is attached to this complaint. 


Requested Action : I respectfully request that your office review this matter and take appropriate enforcement action, including : Investigating the originators advertising practices ; Requiring corrective action to ensure compliance with TILA/Reg Z XXXX Determining whether additional sanctions, fines, or disciplinary measures are warranted.

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

text:
Issue : Sallie Mae is preventing me from opting out of my post-graduation grace period on my private student loan, despite my repeated verbal and written requests to begin principal and interest repayment immediately. This policy is causing substantial financial harm by forcing me to remain in a non-repayment status while interest accrues at an extremely high rate ( XXXX % APR ). 

I have attempted multiple times to initiate full repayment including while speaking to their representatives and was told they would file an internal request to remove the grace period. I received no formal communication or denial letter. I followed up again and was told my request had been denied without any justification or documentation. I have also requested escalation and was ignored.

Sallie Maes own public statements suggest that borrowers may request to end deferment at any time. Yet in practice, they are treating the grace period as non-waivable, blocking me from repaying the loan and simultaneously reporting my account as in grace, which is preventing me from refinancing with other lenders at more favorable interest rates ( such as 5 % ). 

This appears to be an Unfair or Abusive Act or Practice ( UDAAP ) under the CFPBs rules, as it, Causes substantial financial harm by trapping me in high interest accrual, Is not reasonably avoidable, as I have made every effort to begin repayment, Provides no benefit to me as a borrower, and only benefits the lender.

Additionally, their failure to provide a formal written denial or explain their refusal may violate the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) or related disclosure obligations.

I am requesting that : 1.Sallie Mae provide a formal, written explanation for their refusal to remove the grace period, 2.I be allowed to transition into full repayment status immediately, and 3. Sallie Mae be investigated for any patterns of blocking repayment to trap borrowers in high-interest grace periods for profit.

Thank you for your assistance. Im happy to provide supporting documentation or follow up as needed.

sub_issue: Notice to repossess
text:
This complaint concerns an unlawful repossession that occurred on my private property in the State of Florida. The repossession company, acting on behalf of XXXX XXXX XXXX entered my property without my consent, breached the peace, and caused damage to my secured gate in order to retrieve my vehicle. 

On XXXX XXXX the repossession agent forcibly opened my gate and removed the vehicle without prior notice or a valid court order. The incident was captured on my propertys surveillance camera, and a police report has been filed documenting the property damage and unlawful entry. 

Under Florida Statute 679.609 ( 2 ), while a secured party may repossess collateral after default, they must do so without a breach of the peace. Entering a locked or gated property without consent constitutes a clear breach of peace. Any damage to property in the process of repossession further supports that violation.

Additionally, this conduct may constitute violations of : Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692d prohibiting conduct that harasses, oppresses, or abuses any person in connection with debt collection.

FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692f ( 6 ) forbids taking or threatening to take any nonjudicial action to effect dispossession of property if there is no present right to possession or if the property is protected by law.

Uniform Commercial Code 9-609 ( as adopted by Florida law ) restricts repossession to methods that avoid confrontation or property damage.

The repossession companys actions violated my right to peaceful possession and safety on my property. Their actions were reckless, damaging, and illegal under both state and federal consumer protection laws.

Supporting Evidence Copy of the police report documenting the gate damage and trespass.

Video footage from my propertys security camera showing the incident.

Photo of agents on private property after break and entering Photos of the damaged gate.

Video is available per request

In XX/XX/XXXX, my auto loan with Santander Consumer USA was charged off due to financial hardship. I contacted Santander multiple times in XXXX and XXXX requesting information about hardship options, reasonable settlement terms, and whether payment plans were available. 

The vehicle is XXXX XXXX XXXX and has a fair market value of approximately {$6500.00}. I offered a {$6500.00} settlement, payable over XXXX monthly installments, which reflects the cars value and my financial ability. 

Santander refused to consider any hardship accommodation and told me they would only accept an {$8000.00} settlement in XXXX lump sum. They also told me that I must still adhere to the original contract terms, even though the account is already charged off. They refused to offer any payment plan or alternative options and stated {$8000.00} or nothing. 

This response is not consistent with CFPB hardship accommodation guidance ( CFPB XXXX XXXX ), which requires lenders to reasonably evaluate a borrowers hardship and avoid blanket refusals. It is also misleading because charged-off accounts are no longer treated as active installment loans under FCRA, UCC Article XXXX, and general charge-off standards. Santanders statement that I must follow the original contract after charge-off appears inaccurate. 

Their refusal to provide a reasonable settlement option, their insistence on a lump-sum payment that exceeds the vehicles value, and their misrepresentation of my repayment obligations raises concerns under UDAP ( Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ) within the Dodd-Frank Act. 

I am asking for CFPB assistance in obtaining a fair and realistic settlement that aligns with the value of the vehicle, my hardship, and federal consumer protection standards.
